labels.lem:prime-five-exceptional-composition: All five Pfaffians and 25 cofactors reconstructed in the exact GF(2) coefficient ring. Adjugate row/column orientation is correct: adj(M)[i,j] is cofactor(j,i), and division of row zero by s0 gives tau_j. All five compositions have the common polynomial quotient E after division by y_j. Every zero-coordinate specialization is covered by the polynomial identities. The coefficient pivot is exactly c1^4, hence becomes 1; coefficient gcd(E)=1 ensures E never vanishes identically and the proportionality gcd t^5+1 gives precisely the claimed exceptional ratios over an algebraically closed field.
labels.prop:prime-five-empty-common-wall: The previously fully audited prime-five theorem supplies generic dual/multiplication rank four and a birational radical. If Q(y)=0 at a dual-maximal point, the exact composition identity with E proportional to Q gives tau(sigma(y))=0, so every cofactor of M vanishes. Conversely, simultaneous maximal ranks identify s projectively with sigma(y_s); the Euler incidence condition is then exactly Q(y_s)=0. Thus the proposed common maximal-rank wall is empty. No specialization of a full local-system fibre across a rank drop is used.
labels.rem:prime-five-empty-wall-scope: This is an abstract Heisenberg tensor counterexample to a common-wall inference. It preserves generic Euler bijectivity and does not assert actual Cartier realizability, a monodromy counterexample, an abelian-surface embedding, or a classification of the contracted image.
